skill.name: debugging
skill.description: Debugging guidance for error analysis, failed tests, stack traces, logs, root cause analysis, and incident follow-up.
skill.summary: Analyze errors, logs, and failing behavior to identify root causes and practical fixes.

remediation.suggestion: Label code blocks as examples and state that commands should only run with user approval on trusted local files.

remediation.suggestion: Update the references to references/debugging-workflows.md and references/incident-postmortem.template.md for accuracy.

content.value_statement: Debugging complex failures often requires connecting errors, logs, code paths, and recent changes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured process for root cause analysis and practical fixes.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes error messages, stack traces, and failure context.
Guides log parsing with regex examples and a local Python helper script.
Correlates errors across timelines, deployments, and related services.
Identifies common patterns such as null references, timeouts, race conditions, and N+1 queries.
Structures root cause analysis, reproduction steps, minimal fixes, and verification steps.
Provides an incident postmortem template for documenting impact, causes, and action items.
limitations: It depends on accurate logs, stack traces, and reproduction details from the user.
It does not replace production observability, tracing, or incident response tooling.
The helper script only parses local log files supplied by the user.
It cannot prove a fix without running the relevant tests or checks.

use_cases.title: Fix a Failing Test
use_cases.description: Trace a failing unit or integration test to the code path, bad assumption, or changed dependency that caused it.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production Errors
use_cases.description: Group log errors, correlate them with deploys or traffic changes, and form a focused root cause hypothesis.

use_cases.title: Document an Incident
use_cases.description: Turn an outage timeline, impact summary, and corrective actions into a clear postmortem draft.

prompt_templates.title: Explain This Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner debugging of a single error message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug this error and explain the likely cause in plain language: [paste error message and relevant code].

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Failing Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate investigation with test output and source context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this failing test. Use the failure output, stack trace, and related code to identify the root cause and smallest fix.

prompt_templates.title: Find Log Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced log review across repeated errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these logs for recurring errors, timeline patterns, and likely root causes. Separate evidence from hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Run Incident Root Cause Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debugging workflow to analyze this incident. Build a timeline, identify contributing factors, propose fixes, and draft verification steps.

output_examples.input: A JavaScript TypeError appears when a profile page loads.
output: Identifies the failing property access and the function that can return an empty value.
Explains why the assumption failed for a missing user record.
Recommends a null check, clearer error handling, and a regression test.

output_examples.input: PostgreSQL connection errors spike after a deployment.
output: Groups the repeated connection failures by time and service.
Connects the spike to pool exhaustion and missing cleanup paths.
Suggests releasing connections in error paths and validating the fix with load tests.

output_examples.input: A production incident needs a postmortem draft.
output: Creates a timeline from detection through recovery.
Separates customer impact, root cause, and contributing factors.
Lists action items for prevention, detection, and response.

best_practices: Provide the complete error message, stack trace, recent changes, and expected behavior.
Ask for hypotheses with evidence before requesting code changes.
Verify each fix with the smallest relevant test, then run broader regression checks.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad rewrites before the failure point is isolated.
Do not paste secrets, tokens, or private customer data inside logs.
Do not accept a root cause claim without evidence from code, logs, or tests.

faq.question: What kinds of bugs does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with errors, exceptions, failing tests, stack traces, log patterns, production incidents, and recurring system anomalies.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and examples. Any local command or helper script should be run only when the user approves it.

faq.question: Can it analyze production logs?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user provides sanitized logs or a trusted local log file. Sensitive values should be removed first.

faq.question: Does it include a helper script?
faq.answer: Yes. The included Python script parses a local log file and prints grouped error analysis as JSON.

faq.question: Can it write an incident postmortem?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a template for timelines, impact, root cause, corrective actions, and follow-up tasks.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows fit Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they have access to relevant code, logs, and tests.
